items.title: How to calculate the DSO in FSCM - SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
items.author: Brant1
items.text:
There is a Help portal - How the DSO Is Calculated ( https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_CLOUD/918bca53037f408f91a2295d04ac16bc/30759d54da6e420ba745718ef5cfa970.html?version=LATEST&ai=true&locale=en-US ) of Public Cloud, and how can we retrieve the parameters in a Fiori App? 
 If you're wondering how to calculate Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) using the Public Cloud platform, here's an approach you can follow based on a practical example: 
 Example: Calculating DSO on November 19th 
 Today is November 19th , and the DSO is 110 . Let’s break down the calculation step-by-step: 

 Step 1: Retrieve Customer Balance in Fiori App 

 Use the app "Display Customer Balance" in Fiori to get the required financial details. 

 Posting Period : The current posting period is November (Period 11) . 

 Current Balance : The balance displayed for this period is 70,801.57 EUR . 

 Sales of the Period : The total sales for the last three periods need to be calculated as follows: 
 September sales: 70,035.63 EUR 
 October sales: -19.94 EUR 
 November sales: 0 EUR 
 Total Sales for the Period = 70,035.63 + (-19.94) + 0 = 70,015.69 EUR 

 Step 2: Determine the Sales Period 
 The sales period is calculated as the sum of the sales days in the last three months, plus the sales days in the current month (up to today). For this example: 
 September : 31 days 
 October : 30 days 
 November : 31 days 
 Current Month Days until November 19th : 18 or 19 days 
 Note: Due to time zone differences, the value for the current month's sales days can sometimes vary between the actual number of days passed and one less day. In this example, we are using 18 days. 
 Therefore, the total Sales Period = 31 days + 30 days + 31 days + 18 days = 110 days . 
 Step 3: Calculate DSO 
 :The DSO = Currently Balance / (Sales of the Period * period ) = 70801.57/ ( 70,015.69 * 110 )= 111.2346775415625 = 111 

 Hopefully it is helpful for your doubt about calculating the DSO of FSCM. 
 Best Regards, 
 Brant

items.title: Material to spec link for SDS generation in a combined PLM/Product safety environment
items.author: S0027628040
items.text:
I wondered if anyone had tackled this challenge before and, if so, how they addressed it: 
 I'm working in a combined PLM/Product Safety Classic environment - the S/4 version of the ECC EHS and recipe management. We're designing a data structure that will be used for both recipe management and SDS generation and have hit a challenge with assigning materials to specs. Our current data structure is: 
 A spec for the bulk chemical. HALB materials will be assigned to this spec type 
 Specs for the finished goods. Finished goods are a combination of the bulk material and packaging. Bulk and finished goods specs are indirectly connected via the recipe: the recipe for a finished good uses the bulk spec as an input component. A Finished Good general recipe has a corresponding finished good spec. FERT materials will be assigned to finished good specs. there will probably be more than 1 FERT per finished goods spec and more than 1 finished good spec per bulk spec. We can assume that the FERTs have different product names 

 My challenges are: 
 Which object to use for SDS generation 
 Leading on, how to connect the materials to the spec used for SDS generation: I can assume that I'll need SDSs for all the FERTs and probably for the HALB 
 I want to be able to use automatic SDS shipping in the future 
 I'll also be creating European Poison Centre Notifications for the spec where I generate the SDS, using a 3rd party tool. 
 My thoughts: 
 Creating the SDS on the bulk spec makes sense, as the bulk spec contains the Information that I need to create a SDS and also because a SDS is supposed to be Independent of the pack size. Creating PCNs from this spec would also work 
 The crux of the problem: 
 If I generate the SDS on the bulk spec, then in order to get the product name from the FERT material, I need to assign a FERT material to a bulk spec. This results in 1 FERT being assigned to 2 specs; 1 finished good spec and one bulk spec. This is not great and will trigger the need to customise all cases where a material needs to find a spec e.g. automatic SDS shipping, SVT 
 An alternative option would be to create inheritance relationships between the bulk and finished goods specs and generate SDSs on the finished goods specs. The would mean that 1 material was assigned to one spec. However this could lead to duplicate SDSs because multiple FERTs have the same product name but different packaging and also the need for a SDS for the HALB. 
 Neither option looks great. Has anyone tackled a similar situation and how did they address it? Are there other options that I'm missing? 
 Thanks 
 Phil

By now, you may have read our introduction to organizational modeling in SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central or the 2H 2026 release post on how it closes the gap between workforce strategy and execution . Those blogs cover what the capability does and why it was built. This one is about what comes next for you. 
 Organizational modeling is now generally available in SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central, included in your subscription at no additional cost. For many organizations, the question has shifted from "what is this?" to "how do we actually get going?" Two resources are designed to answer exactly that. 
 See it in action first 
 Before activating any new capability, it helps to see it working in a real context. The 10-minute SAP SuccessFactors Organizational Modeling Demo walks you through the full end-to-end experience: creating a modeling project, running simulations with drag-and-drop and list views, reviewing the impact of proposed changes, and publishing the approved scenario back to your live Employee Central structure.

 Then follow the step-by-step infographic

 Download the infographic

Teams can run multiple simulation versions, compare scenarios, and apply the approved outcome through a controlled cascading save that propagates changes across related organizational objects, including legal entity, business unit, division, department, cost center, and position.

items.title: Relembre a palestra: Aprendendo durante a jornada, da logística ao SAP EWM #SITCWB2026
items.author: AdrianoCWB
items.text:
No dia 7 de novembro, no Auditório Gregor Mendel da PUCPR, Natalia Dyna, Consultora WMS da Simple WMS, apresentou no SAP Inside Track Curitiba 2026 a palestra "Aprendendo durante a jornada: logística de armazéns dos clientes do ecossistema SAP". 
 Sobre a palestra 
 Natalia contou como chegou ao SAP vindo da operação logística: frota, armazenagem e transporte, estoque e liderança. Depois veio a função de coordenação e key user de cadastros SAP, até a entrada na Simple WMS, em 2025, como consultora SAP EWM/WMS. 
 A porta de entrada foi uma sequência de oportunidade, inscrição, seleção e formação com dinâmicas. Em suas palavras, ela teve a chance de continuar com o "não" ou tentar o "sim", e tentou o sim. 
 Como um consultor se prepara 
 Teoria: ensino a distância, SAP Learning Hub, apostilas e livros da SAP Press. 
 Feedback: líder, sênior e mentoria. 
 Prática: atividade em projeto, acompanhamento de um consultor (sombra), testes e configuração. 
 O que o consultor realmente faz 
 Natalia resumiu a base do consultor em quatro verbos: ouvir, ensinar, traduzir e acompanhar. O consultor não entrega só configuração, ele muda a forma como o cliente trabalha. Isso começa por respeitar o investimento que o cliente fez no sistema. 
 Cada operação tem sua realidade 
 Mesmo sistema, armazéns muito diferentes: ela mostrou operações em Maracanaú (CE), Águas de Santa Bárbara (SP) e Conde (PB). O sistema é igual, as pessoas e a cultura não são. A pergunta que ficou: é simples para quem configura, mas é simples para quem usa? Alguém com 30 anos de empresa que nunca usou um coletor aprende como alguém que chegou agora? 
 Daí a importância de ir ao Gemba, palavra japonesa para "o local onde as coisas acontecem", incluindo uma visita a uma câmara fria. Lá se avalia o processo (o atual suporta o SAP standard?) e a tecnologia (o sistema reflete o processo de verdade?). 
 Para levar 
 Tecnologia é o meio, o processo é o caminho e a transformação acontece com as pessoas. 
 Quem está disposto a aprender está pronto para evoluir. 
 Perguntas para a plateia: onde você quer chegar, o que está fazendo para chegar lá e você desiste no primeiro "não"? 
 Sobre a palestrante e o patrocínio 
 Natalia Dyna, Consultora WMS da Simple WMS. 
 A Simple WMS foi patrocinadora Bronze do SAP Inside Track Curitiba 2026.

items.title: Who Wins the Next Disruption: Five Rules for Creating Supply Chains that Can Take a Hit
items.author: Oyku Ilgar
items.text:
When a major supply chain disruption hits, the winners are rarely the companies that predicted it. The winners are the ones that are quickest in deciding how to best react to it. 
 Orchestrate your supply chain to stay ahead and exceed expectations 

 Learn how 

 It is one of the simplest ways to think about supply chain resilience today, and a central theme of the latest Future of Supply Chain podcast episode with Kearney’s Rudolph Lohmeyer and Jeff Greer. 

 For years, resilience was treated primarily as a question of protection. How much inventory should we hold? How many suppliers should we have? Where should we build capacity? How much redundancy can we afford? 

 These questions still matter, but no company can prepare for everything. 

 For decades, global supply chains were designed around stability. That model is now being tested on multiple fronts. Geopolitical tension, environmental disruption, armed conflict, technological advances, and shifting trade relationships all shape how goods move, where they are made, and at what cost. 

 The bigger question is whether organizations can recognize when something changes, understand what it means to their business and make a timely decision. 

 And disruption does not always mean bad news. One company’s supply chain problem can become another company’s opportunity. As Rudolph Lohmeyer, senior partner at Kearney and the leader of Kearney Foresight, puts it: “Countries and companies actually see that to the extent that they can position themselves to be effective in this environment, they can create advantage because these shocks are reallocating value.” 

 The goal is not to build a supply chain that never gets hit, but to build one that can take a hit, adapt, and keep moving. 

 Here are five rules to keep in mind. 

 Rule 1: Know where resilience creates the most value 

 The instinctive response to uncertainty is often defensive: build more inventory, find another supplier, add manufacturing capacity. Each can be sensible. None is free. 

 Principal Jeff Greer explained: “From a supply chain standpoint, resilience is capital-intensive. Companies can build redundant manufacturing capacity and diversify supply across the globe. But they have to balance the cost, working capital, and risk exposure. You don’t need maximum redundancy. You need resilience where it matters most.” 

 The question, then, is not how much redundancy a company can build, but where that redundancy will actually make a difference. 

 Answering that requires knowing where a supply chain is genuinely exposed, which means seeing the full network. Many companies still cannot see far enough into their own. Greer added: “Most companies lack a reliable, end-to-end view of their supply chain ecosystem and the dependencies within it. That makes it extremely difficult to not only to identify an external shock, but, more importantly, to understand its business impact and determine what to do about it.” 

 Most companies know their direct suppliers. But what about the suppliers behind them? What happens if a critical component comes from a single factory that nobody in the organization has been tracking? How quickly would you find out? 

 Lohmeyer compared this complexity to the financial instruments at the heart of the global financial crisis: layers of dependencies that look manageable until something goes wrong. 

 Rule 2: Focus on the shocks that matter most 

 If the future is uncertain, why not model every possible risk? Because there are too many of them, and the most consequential are often the ones nobody saw coming. Geopolitical conflict, trade restrictions, cyberattacks, new regulations, supplier failures, environmental disruptions: The list is long. 

 As Lohmeyer explained, rather than boiling the ocean, organizations should identify a manageable set of strategic shocks across social, technological, economic, environmental, and geopolitical domains. He added: “Understand across that range the universe that could occur and then prioritize down within it that which would most affect an organization.” 

 There is also a difference between a shock and a scenario. A shock is a discrete event, such as Fukushima or the initial outbreak of COVID-19. A scenario describes the broader environment in which a business may have to operate. One demands a response. The other shapes the capabilities needed to stay resilient over time. 

 As Lohmeyer added, the goal is not to “reduce uncertainty and predict the future” but to “manage it and map it.” 

 Rule 3: Turn signals into options before they disappear 

 AI can shorten the distance between seeing a problem and responding to it. 

 Digital twins can model global supply networks and test how they might respond to different shocks. Advanced analytics can surface patterns across large volumes of data. AI can continuously monitor signals ranging from geopolitical events and tariffs to weather, commodity prices, supplier health and regulatory changes. 

 “AI agents can increasingly connect to planning and execution systems, allowing companies to run scenarios, identify thresholds, and take pre-approved actions while keeping humans in the loop,” Greer noted. “Now we have the ability to take these agents, tap them into the planning and execution systems so that speed to respond is ever-increasing.” 

 This matters because supply chain alternatives have a shelf life. A supplier may have capacity today that is gone tomorrow. A logistics route may be open until demand surges. A manufacturing alternative may hold until the next disruption closes it. 

 Lohmeyer added: “AI allows for a computational power that allows you to consider intersections and sequences in such a high-resolution way that we’re able to approach that work entirely differently and much more effectively. Not just faster, but better.” 

 But technology can only take an organization so far. 

 Rule 4: Technology alone does not make an organization adaptable 

 A digital twin cannot approve a supplier switch. An AI model cannot decide which trade-offs the business is willing to accept. A dashboard cannot decide what the company is willing to sacrifice to put things right. 

 Lohmeyer explained: “The ability of AI to compute pathways and sequences at massive scale gives the ability to map uncertainty in a much higher resolution way. You still require the human intelligence to understand. How do we form solutions, mobilize teams to be ready to respond? How do we build the capabilities, people, process, technologies to be able to respond? 

 That puts the focus squarely on the operating model behind the technology. Who has the authority to make the call? When does a potential disruption trigger escalation? Which actions are pre-approved? Who owns the data? Which teams need to be involved? 

 Relationships matter too. Strong supplier relationships enable faster information sharing, pre-agreed responses, and genuine diversification rather than simply duplicating capacity everywhere. 

 Technology can make the analysis faster. The organization still has to be capable of acting on it. 

 Rule 5: Build for what is coming, not just for what has happened 

 The hardest part of resilience is preparing for something you have never seen before. That means looking beyond the last disruption and paying attention to what is shifting around the business: technology, regulation, supplier markets, and climate patterns. 

 Lohmeyer described it this way: “That the future of supply chain will occur by understanding the reality that’s coming but is not yet here.” 

 Instead of asking what to do if a given event happens, companies can ask a more useful question: What is changing now and what could it mean for us? That shift matters because the next disruption may not look like the last one. 

 As Lohmeyer put it, “Those that can compress that and make highest quality decisions at speed are those who will win.” 

 Resilience is not about building a supply chain that can be protected from everything. That is impossible. The goal is to design one that can take a hit, understand what the disruption changes, and act while it still has options. 

 To hear the full conversation, tune in to the Future of Supply Chain podcast: Building Supply Chains That Can Take a Hit .

items.title: EEE :Custom Business Event for Billing Document Creation with Custom Payload and Context Filters
items.author: ritesh_9898
items.text:
Technical Specification & Implementation Guide 
 Custom Business Event for Billing Document Creation with Custom Payload and Context Filters 
 1. Solution Architecture Overview 
 This solution establishes a hybrid integration pattern in SAP S/4HANA: billing document creation events trigger a custom workflow receiver function module via Event Type Linkage ( SWE2 ), which filters business transactions, validates sales order references, enriches header data using released Core Data Services (CDS), and raises an ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP) Business Event . 
 The event is bound via an Event Binding artifact ( .evtbnd ) and published to external event brokers (such as SAP Event Mesh / SAP Integration Suite, Advanced Event Mesh) using SAP Enterprise Event Enablement ( /IWXBE/ ), utilizing context annotations for source-side topic filtering. 
 ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ SD Billing Creation (e.g. VF01) │
└────────────────┬────────────────┘
 │ Raises Event CREATED (Class CL_SD_BIL_BD_EVENT / VBRK)
 ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐ SWE2 Event Type Linkage
│ SWE2 Event Linkage ├──────────────────────────┐
└─────────────────────────────────┘ │
 ▼
 ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Receiver Function Module │
 │ ZSWW_WI_CREATE_VIA_EVENT_IBF │
 └───────────────┬─────────────────┘
 │ Validates & reads I_BillingDocument
 ▼
 ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Behavior Pool Class │
 │ ZBP_I_BILLINGDOCCREATED │
 │ (RAISE ENTITY EVENT) │
 └───────────────┬─────────────────┘
 │
 ▼
 ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
 │ RAP Business Event │
 │ ZI_BillingDocCreated~Created │
 └───────────────┬─────────────────┘
 │ Mapped via Event Binding (Z_SALES_INV)
 ▼
 ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Enterprise Event Enablement │
 │ (/IWXBE/OUTBOUND_CFG) │
 └───────────────┬─────────────────┘
 │ Source-side Filtering (/IWXBE/EVENT_FILTER)
 ▼
 ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
 │ SAP Event Mesh / AEM Broker │
 │ (oneerp/Invoice/Created/v1) │
 └─────────────────────────────────┘ 
 2. Step 1: Trace Billing Document Creation Event (SWELS / SWEL) 
 Before configuring the receiver module, verify that the event is actively triggered in the system during billing document generation. In modern SAP S/4HANA systems, this event is published by the ABAP Class CL_SD_BIL_BD_EVENT (as well as legacy BOR VBRK ). 
 Activate Event Trace ( SWELS ) : Execute transaction SWELS and turn Event Trace to Switch On . 
 Execute Business Transaction : Create and post a billing document using transaction VF01 . 
 Verify Event Log in SWEL : Filter by Object Category CL ABAP Class , Object Type CL_SD_BIL_BD_EVENT , and Event CREATED . 
 Figure 1: SWEL Event Trace displaying CL_SD_BIL_BD_EVENT CREATED event 
 Deactivate Event Trace ( SWELS ) : Turn off trace logging after validation. 
 3. Step 2: Data Model Creation (CDS Entities) 
 3.1 Root View Entity: ZI_BillingDocCreated 
 This CDS root view entity serves as the root business object for the event, selecting from released view I_BillingDocument . 
 @AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED
@EndUserText.label: 'Billing Document Created - Root Entity'
define root view entity ZI_BillingDocCreated
 as select from I_BillingDocument
{
 // Event subject key
 key BillingDocument,

 // Payload fields
 SDDocumentCategory,
 BillingDocumentType,
 OverallBillingStatus,
 BillingIssueType,
 BillingDocumentCategory,
 PayerParty,
 SoldToParty,
 SalesOrganization,
 DistributionChannel
} 
 3.2 Abstract Entity: ZD_BillingDocCreated (Payload & Context Filters) 
 This abstract entity defines the payload structure. The @event .context annotations expose context attributes directly into the CloudEvents metadata headers for source-side filtering. 
 @EndUserText.label: 'Billing Document Created - Event Payload'
define abstract entity ZD_BillingDocCreated
{
 SDDocumentCategory : vbtypl;

 @Event.context : { attribute: 'xsapbilltype', position: 1 }
 BillingDocumentType : fkart;

 OverallBillingStatus : vf_status;
 BillingIssueType : vf_todo;
 BillingDocumentCategory : fktyp;
 PayerParty : kunrg;
 SoldToParty : kunag;

 @Event.context : { attribute: 'xsapsalesorg', position: 2 }
 SalesOrganization : vkorg;

 DistributionChannel : vtweg;
} 
 4. Step 3: Behavior Definition (BDEF) 
 Declare the custom business event within the Behavior Definition for ZI_BillingDocCreated . 
 managed with unmanaged save implementation in class zbp_i_billingdoccreated unique;
strict ( 2 );

define behavior for ZI_BillingDocCreated
lock master
authorization master ( instance )
{
 // Declare the custom business event with the payload parameter
 event Created parameter ZD_BillingDocCreated;
} 
 5. Step 4: Behavior Pool Class (ZBP_I_BILLINGDOCCREATED) 
 RAISE ENTITY EVENT is restricted to behavior implementation classes. A public static wrapper method delegates the call to a local handler class within the behavior pool. 
 5.1 Global Class Definition & Implementation 
 CLASS zbp_i_billingdoccreated DEFINITION
 PUBLIC
 ABSTRACT
 FINAL
 FOR BEHAVIOR OF zi_billingdoccreated.

 PUBLIC SECTION.
 " Event parameter table for external callers
 TYPES tt_created TYPE TABLE FOR EVENT zi_billingdoccreated~created.

 " Public static API to trigger the event from outside the behavior pool
 CLASS-METHODS raise_created
 IMPORTING
 it_events TYPE tt_created.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS zbp_i_billingdoccreated IMPLEMENTATION.

 METHOD raise_created.
 lcl_event_handler=>on_created( it_events ).
 ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS. 
 5.2 Local Types Definition & Implementation (Local Include) 
 CLASS lhc_zi_billingdoccreated DEFINITION INHERITING FROM cl_abap_behavior_handler.
 PRIVATE SECTION.
 METHODS get_instance_authorizations FOR INSTANCE AUTHORIZATION
 IMPORTING keys REQUEST requested_authorizations FOR ZI_BillingDocCreated RESULT result.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lhc_zi_billingdoccreated IMPLEMENTATION.
 METHOD get_instance_authorizations.
 ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_event_handler DEFINITION FRIENDS zbp_i_billingdoccreated.
 PUBLIC SECTION.
 CLASS-METHODS on_created
 IMPORTING
 it_events TYPE zbp_i_billingdoccreated=>tt_created.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_event_handler IMPLEMENTATION.
 METHOD on_created.
 " Raise the RAP business event
 RAISE ENTITY EVENT ZI_BillingDocCreated~Created FROM it_events.
 ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS. 
 6. Step 5: Event Binding Configuration (.evtbnd) 
 In ABAP Development Tools (ADT): 
 Create a new Event Binding named Z_SALES_INV . 
 Set Type Namespace : oneerp , SAP Object Type : Invoice , Operation : Created . 
 Add version 0001.0.0 bound to Entity ZI_BILLINGDOCCREATED and Entity Event CREATED . 
 Activate the artifact. 
 Figure 2: Event Binding Z_SALES_INV configured in ABAP Development Tools (ADT) 
 7. Step 6: Workflow Receiver Function Module (ZSWW_WI_CREATE_VIA_EVENT_IBF) 
 This function module is called by the event linkage. It validates business rules, extracts billing header data via released CDS view I_BillingDocument , populates the payload, and dispatches the event. You can write your own business logic here for trigger RAP event.. 
 FUNCTION zsww_wi_create_via_event_ibf.
*"----------------------------------------------------------------------
*"*"Local Interface:
*" IMPORTING
*" VALUE(SENDER) TYPE SIBFLPORB
*" VALUE(EVENT) TYPE SIBFEVENT
*" VALUE(RECTYPE) TYPE SWFERECTYP
*" VALUE(HANDLER) TYPE SIBFLPORB
*" VALUE(EXCEPTIONS_ALLOWED) TYPE SWEFLAGS-EXC_OK DEFAULT SPACE
*" VALUE(XML_SIZE) TYPE SWF_XMLSIZ
*" VALUE(EVENT_CONTAINER) TYPE SWF_XMLCNT
*" EXPORTING
*" VALUE(RESULT) TYPE SWFREVRSLT
*" EXCEPTIONS
*" READ_FAILED
*" CREATE_FAILED
*"----------------------------------------------------------------------

 CONSTANTS: lc_elem_evt_objkey TYPE swfdname VALUE '_EVT_OBJKEY',
 lc_elem_tcode TYPE swfdname VALUE '_TCODE',
 lc_tcode_vf01 TYPE tcode VALUE 'VF01',
 lc_typeid_vbrk TYPE sibftypeid VALUE 'VBRK',
 lc_typeid_class TYPE sibftypeid VALUE 'CL_SD_BIL_BD_EVENT'.

 TYPES: BEGIN OF lty_billing_header,
 sddocumentcategory TYPE i_billingdocument-sddocumentcategory,
 billingdocumenttype TYPE i_billingdocument-billingdocumenttype,
 overallbillingstatus TYPE i_billingdocument-overallbillingstatus,
 billingissuetype TYPE i_billingdocument-billingissuetype,
 billingdocumentcategory TYPE i_billingdocument-billingdocumentcategory,
 payerparty TYPE i_billingdocument-payerparty,
 soldtoparty TYPE i_billingdocument-soldtoparty,
 salesorganization TYPE i_billingdocument-salesorganization,
 distributionchannel TYPE i_billingdocument-distributionchannel,
 END OF lty_billing_header.

 DATA: lwa_billing_header TYPE lty_billing_header,
 l_evt_objkey TYPE swo_typeid,
 l_tcode TYPE tcode,
 l_invoice TYPE vbeln_vf,
 l_sales_order TYPE vbeln_va,
 lo_event_container TYPE REF TO cl_swf_cnt_container,
 lt_svo_event TYPE zbp_i_billingdoccreated=>tt_created.

 CLEAR result.

 " 1. Reconstruct event container from XML
 TRY.
 lo_event_container = cl_swf_cnt_factory=>create_from_xml(
 im_xml_table = event_container
 im_xml_size = xml_size ).
 CATCH cx_swf_cnt_container.
 CLEAR lo_event_container.
 ENDTRY.

 IF lo_event_container IS NOT BOUND.
 IF exceptions_allowed = abap_true.
 RAISE read_failed.
 ENDIF.
 RETURN.
 ENDIF.

 " 2. Extract Event Parameters via Public Interface
 TRY.
 lo_event_container->if_swf_ifs_parameter_container=>get(
 EXPORTING name = lc_elem_evt_objkey
 IMPORTING value = l_evt_objkey ).
 CATCH cx_swf_cnt_container.
 CLEAR l_evt_objkey.
 ENDTRY.

 TRY.
 lo_event_container->if_swf_ifs_parameter_container=>get(
 EXPORTING name = lc_elem_tcode
 IMPORTING value = l_tcode ).
 CATCH cx_swf_cnt_container.
 CLEAR l_tcode.
 ENDTRY.

 " Fallback: sender instance ID carries the key
 IF l_evt_objkey IS INITIAL AND ( sender-typeid = lc_typeid_vbrk OR sender-typeid = lc_typeid_class ).
 l_evt_objkey = sender-instid.
 ENDIF.

 " 3. Transaction Gate: Process VF01 creations (allow empty tcode for background jobs)
 IF ( l_tcode <> lc_tcode_vf01 AND l_tcode IS NOT INITIAL ) OR l_evt_objkey IS INITIAL.
 RETURN.
 ENDIF.

 l_invoice = |{ l_evt_objkey(10) ALPHA = IN }|.

 " 4. Business Validation: Verify invoice references a sales document
 SELECT SINGLE salesdocument
 FROM i_billingdocumentitem
 WHERE billingdocument = @l_invoice
 AND salesdocument <> @space
 INTO @l_sales_order.
 IF sy-subrc <> 0.
 RETURN.
 ENDIF.

 " 5. Retrieve Invoice Header Data from Released CDS View
 SELECT SINGLE sddocumentcategory,
 billingdocumenttype,
 overallbillingstatus,
 billingissuetype,
 billingdocumentcategory,
 payerparty,
 soldtoparty,
 salesorganization,
 distributionchannel
 FROM i_billingdocument
 WHERE billingdocument = @l_invoice
 INTO CORRESPONDING FIELDS OF @lwa_billing_header.

 IF sy-subrc <> 0.
 IF exceptions_allowed = abap_true.
 RAISE read_failed.
 ENDIF.
 RETURN.
 ENDIF.

 " 6. Construct Payload and Raise RAP Business Event
 lt_svo_event = VALUE #(
 ( billingdocument = l_invoice
 %param = VALUE #( sddocumentcategory = lwa_billing_header-sddocumentcategory
 billingdocumenttype = lwa_billing_header-billingdocumenttype
 overallbillingstatus = lwa_billing_header-overallbillingstatus
 billingissuetype = lwa_billing_header-billingissuetype
 billingdocumentcategory = lwa_billing_header-billingdocumentcategory
 payerparty = lwa_billing_header-payerparty
 soldtoparty = lwa_billing_header-soldtoparty
 salesorganization = lwa_billing_header-salesorganization
 distributionchannel = lwa_billing_header-distributionchannel ) ) ).

 zbp_i_billingdoccreated=>raise_created( it_events = lt_svo_event ).

ENDFUNCTION. 
 8. Step 7: SWE2 Event Type Linkage Configuration 
 Configure the linkage entry in transaction SWE2 as shown below: 
 Field Configuration Value Description 
 Object Category CL ABAP Class ABAP Class based event linkage 
 Object Type CL_SD_BIL_BD_EVENT Standard Billing Document Event Class 
 Event CREATED Billing document creation event 
 Receiver Type ZAIF_EVENT Custom receiver identifier 
 Receiver Call Function Module Function module dispatch method 
 Receiver Function Module ZSWW_WI_CREATE_VIA_EVENT_IBF Custom receiver function modul

items.title: Replicate Work Center from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Edition to SAP Field Service & Asset Management
items.author: Saurabh_Awasthi85
items.text:
In Maintenance and service-based industries, having the right people and resources in the right place is important to keep work running smoothly and on time. Organizations using SAP S/4HANA Cloud Edition use Work Centers to define the teams, workshops, and resources responsible for maintenance activities. They also maintain details such as available working hours, capacity, and responsibilities. However, when dispatchers and field technicians use SAP Field Service & Asset Management (FSA), they may not always have clear information about which Work Center is responsible for a particular job in S/4HANA Cloud Edition. This can lead to work being assigned to the wrong team, scheduling issues, and unnecessary communication between the office and field teams. 
 So, what is the solution? 
 Integrate SAP S/4HANA with SAP FSA. 
 By automatically replicating Work Centers from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Edition to SAP Field Service & Asset Management, both systems stay in sync. This helps dispatchers assign work to the right teams and resources, making planning and scheduling easier, faster, and more accurate. 
 Why Does This Integration Matter? 
 With integration: 
 The relevant work centers are already available in FSA immediately when created in S/4HANA Cloud Edition. 
 Faster scheduling, fewer wrong assignments, and a planning picture that matches the backend . 
 Key Benefits of Integration 
 Automatic synchronization of work center master data between S/4HANA and FSA. 
 Consistent resource model delivery. 
 Multi-company support - replicate to one or many FSA companies. 
 Scope of the Integration 
 Here's what's included in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Edition 2702 release. 
 Replication from SAP S/4HANA to SAP FSA is supported. 
 Create or change work centers in S/4HANA CE (Fiori App: “Manage Work Center’). 
 Changes automatically replicate to FSA. 
 Supports both a bulk initial load and incremental (delta) updates on change. 
 FSA Multi-company Support 
 Prerequisites 
 Communication Arrangements with Deployment scenario ID SAP_COM_0B12 is active in the system. DRF Replication Model name is provided in additional properties. 
 Configuration Steps 
 Go to the Fiori app Communication Arrangements and check for scenario id SAP_COM_0B12 

 Add any Replication Model Name in Additional Properties and Save 

 Go to the Fiori App Manage your Solutions 

 Input Application area: Field Service & Asset Management 

 Click on Define replication Rules: Configure 

 Select the Work Center Replication Rule 'WC' 

 The integration Supports Plant and All companies rule type which can be configured from here 
 '01' Belongs to Plant 
 '00' Belongs to All companies 
 Define the Respective Company Name and Assign Company Details 

 For plant-based execution select the corresponding replication object 'WC' 

 Assign Required Plant in section ‘ Assign Relevant Plants’ 

 Work Center Replication Demo 
 Scenario: Once a Work Center is created or changed in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Edition it is automatically replicated to SAP Field Service & Asset Management. 
 Go to the Fiori App ‘ Manage Work Centers ’ and Create/Change work center 

 Click On Create 

 Input Work Center details 

 Click on 'Save' Work center created 

 Check Replication in SAP FSA as Service Regions 

 Check log in app Message Monitoring Overview 
 AIF Namespace: /FSMPM 
 AIF Interface: WORKCT_OUT 
 Final Thoughts 
 Replicating Work Centers from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Edition to FSA keeps the resource model consistent across back office and field. Dispatchers plan against the same crews and workshops in S/4HANA, assignments land with the right team the first time, and the planning picture always reflects the backend — no manual re-keying, no guesswork. 
 With master data in sync, scheduling gets sharper, technicians get clearer direction, and the whole service operation runs a little smoother.

items.title: How to calculate the DSO in FSCM - SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
items.author: Brant1
items.text:
There is a Help portal - How the DSO Is Calculated ( https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_CLOUD/918bca53037f408f91a2295d04ac16bc/30759d54da6e420ba745718ef5cfa970.html?version=LATEST&ai=true&locale=en-US ) of Public Cloud, and how can we retrieve the parameters in a Fiori App? 
 If you're wondering how to calculate Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) using the Public Cloud platform, here's an approach you can follow based on a practical example: 
 Example: Calculating DSO on November 19th 
 Today is November 19th , and the DSO is 110 . Let’s break down the calculation step-by-step: 

 Step 1: Retrieve Customer Balance in Fiori App 

 Use the app "Display Customer Balance" in Fiori to get the required financial details. 

 Posting Period : The current posting period is November (Period 11) . 

 Current Balance : The balance displayed for this period is 70,801.57 EUR . 

 Sales of the Period : The total sales for the last three periods need to be calculated as follows: 
 September sales: 70,035.63 EUR 
 October sales: -19.94 EUR 
 November sales: 0 EUR 
 Total Sales for the Period = 70,035.63 + (-19.94) + 0 = 70,015.69 EUR 

 Step 2: Determine the Sales Period 
 The sales period is calculated as the sum of the sales days in the last three months, plus the sales days in the current month (up to today). For this example: 
 September : 31 days 
 October : 30 days 
 November : 31 days 
 Current Month Days until November 19th : 18 or 19 days 
 Note: Due to time zone differences, the value for the current month's sales days can sometimes vary between the actual number of days passed and one less day. In this example, we are using 18 days. 
 Therefore, the total Sales Period = 31 days + 30 days + 31 days + 18 days = 110 days . 
 Step 3: Calculate DSO 
 :The DSO = Currently Balance / (Sales of the Period * period ) = 70801.57/ ( 70,015.69 * 110 )= 111.2346775415625 = 111 

 Hopefully it is helpful for your doubt about calculating the DSO of FSCM. 
 Best Regards, 
 Brant

 We are facing an issue in SAP while clicking the Print Preview option for Project Purchase Orders with Account Assignment Category Q (Project) .

 In case of split valuation, please enter a valuation type

 The issue started occurring after 09.11.2026 . 
 For end users when they click the print preview the system displays purchasing document not yet released, but all the doc are released and checked. Meanwhile when we opened the same PO and click the print preview this message is displayed "In case of split valuation, please enter a valuation type" 
 Expected Behaviour 
 When clicking Print Preview for a Project PO with Account Assignment Category Q, the system should display the PO output preview without triggering the split valuation message. 
 Support Required 
 Could anyone please guide us on why SAP is triggering split valuation validation during Print Preview for Project POs with Account Assignment Category Q, even though split valuation is not maintained for any materials in the client's system? 
 We would appreciate guidance on: 

 What triggers split valuation validation during PO Print Preview?

items.author: Okada0630
items.text:
SAPエキスパートの皆様、こんにちは。 
 以下のSAPノートに基づき、単一明細項目のドキュメントに対する税金計算ロジックを理解しました。 
 SAP Note 80977 - 総額からの税計算、税の四捨五入計算: パート 1 
 リンク: 80977 - 税込価格額からの税計算、税の丸め計算: パート 1 - SAP for Me 
 しかしながら、このSAPノートに記載されている計算ロジックでは説明できない、複数の明細項目を含むケースに遭遇しました。 
 例えば、税コード N2（税率10%、控除額80%） の総額 10円 を考えてみましょう。 
 SAPノート80977に記載されている計算ロジックによると、10円の最終的な正味金額は 10円 です。 
 実際のSAPシステムでもこの動作を確認しました。税コードN2を使用して1行10円の明細を含む伝票を転記すると、結果として得られる正味金額は 10円に なります。 
 しかし、同じ文書に複数の明細項目を登録すると、異なる結果になります。 
 合計金額は 1,111円 で、以下の3つの明細項目から構成されており、すべて税コードN2が適用されます。 
 項目１：10 円 
 項目2： 101円 
 項目3： 1,000円 
 この場合、最初の明細項目である10円の最終的な正味金額は、 10円ではなく 9円 となります。 
 同じ伝票に複数の明細項目が記載されている場合、10円の明細項目が最終的に9円になる理由を説明していただけますか？ 
 特に、SAPが 複数の明細項目にわたって丸め誤差調整、税金配分、または伝票レベルの調整 を実行しているかどうか、また、実行している場合、SAPはどのようにしてその差額を割り当てる明細項目を決定するのかを理解したいと考えています。 
 私の質問をお読みいただき、ありがとうございます。 
 ご意見やご感想をお待ちしております。

items.title: Any chance to implement an ignore feature?
items.author: VXLozano
items.text:
It's the Age of Visibility. People think that if they don't post often, they will be ignored (like if that was a bad thing). 
 It's also the Age of AI. Everybody and their mother are able to put four words toguether about almost anything and sound sound. 
 Both ages came simultaneously, so my feed from the community has been lately a bunch of trivial blog posts about things everybody knew when the original poster was born, and comments about how useful that crup is, almost always with a "community hook" last phrase. 
 I'm not (fully) against the AI use to refine an article. And I'm not (fully) against people needing to be visible, mostly because they think (and maybe they're right) their jobs could depend on that visibility. 
 But I'm against a bloated feed list, and I'm against to have to waste my time here filtering who is writing interesting stuff and who's just farming reputation. 
 I thought an "ignore" button would allow me to lighten that feed. 
 I know, you've not been able to resuscitate the "follow" button, how dare I to ask for an "ignore" one? But to ask is free, and you're always asking for feedback and suggestions. 

 Oh! If you are tired to read mine, just use the ignore button and do it! *wink, wink*

1.summary: A short blog describing a SAP Integration Suite (CPI) scenario in which a CSV file has extra unnamed columns that do not match the expected structure. The author says they used Groovy to assign temporary field names and then passed the data through an OData service into an ABAP custom table. The text gives the problem and the general approach but no code, mapping logic, OData entity names, or error handling. The 'practical considerations' the intro promises are not in the excerpt.
key_points: Problem: CSV rows contain extra, unnamed columns beyond the expected header structure.
Approach: a Groovy script in CPI assigns temporary names to the columns before the payload is sent.
Target: an OData service writes the data into an ABAP custom table.
The excerpt contains no Groovy code, no OData service or entity names, and no ABAP table details.
technical_details: SAP Integration Suite / Cloud Integration (CPI)
Groovy script step for CSV parsing
OData service exposing an ABAP custom table (no names given)
1.why_it_matters: Handling ragged CSV input is a real, common CPI problem, so the topic is relevant. As written, though, the post is an outline and cannot be applied without the details it leaves out.
1.developer_problem: How do I handle CSV rows with unexpected unnamed extra columns in CPI before posting them to an OData-backed ABAP table?
1.teaching_angle: Use it as a discussion prompt: how should a pipeline treat rows with extra columns (reject, truncate, or map to a catch-all field)? Ask learners to write the Groovy step themselves and to decide where validation belongs (CPI or the ABAP side).

20.summary: A developer asks whether passing data to a class by value or by reference matters for memory when moving classic SMOD/CMOD IDoc exit logic (EXIT_SAPLVEDF_002, INVOIC02) into OO code. They propose changing the IMPORTING parameters of an interface method from typed values (vbdkr, nast, edidc, vbdpr_tt, komv_t) to REF TO. They quote SAP's 'copy-on-write sharing' idea and ask whether it holds in every case and whether global data of SAP programs can be passed by reference. The post is a question, not a solution.
key_points: The post compares by-value IMPORTING with REF TO IMPORTING for the same structures and tables.
The author relies on 'copy-on-write sharing' to argue that no copy happens while data is unchanged.
Using REF TO does not remove copying on its own. A copy still happens when the object writes to data it holds, or when a value is stored into an attribute.
The bigger risk with REF TO is semantic: the object sees later changes made by the caller, and it can hold stale or shared state across repeated exit calls.
The post asks about passing global data of SAP programs by reference. That creates hidden coupling to the caller's data lifetime.
technical_details: Interface zif_sd_bill_exit_saplvedf_002 with INTERFACES zif_enhancement and zif_injectable
Method set_data IMPORTING typed as vbdkr, nast, edidc, vbdpr_tt, komv_t (by value vs REF TO)
Method execute with VALUE(is_current_segment) TYPE edidd and CHANGING ct_idoc_data TYPE idoc_data
Exit EXIT_SAPLVEDF_002 in SMOD/CMOD, IDoc INVOIC02, called several times per invoice
Instance attributes in the helper class holding the copied data
20.why_it_matters: Memory and copy behaviour matter in exits that run many times per document. But the post's conclusion that memory is not a concern is too strong. A lower-memory signature can introduce aliasing bugs that are harder to find than the memory cost it avoids.
20.developer_problem: Does passing structures and tables by REF TO avoid memory copies in an OO enhancement class, and is copy-on-write sharing a safe assumption?
20.teaching_angle: Good for an advanced session on ABAP value semantics. Demonstrate with a small program: change the caller's table after set_data and show the object seeing the change under REF TO. Then discuss when a copy really occurs and why design clarity usually beats micro-optimisation here. Treat the 'copy-on-write' claim as an implementation detail to verify, not a language guarantee.

30.summary: A short blog introducing SUBMIT ... USER ... VIA JOB as a way to run an ABAP report under another user's identity through a background job, without sharing that user's password. It names authorization object S_BTCH_NA1 as the control that keeps this secure and auditable. The excerpt gives no syntax examples, no job setup steps, and no details of the authorization fields or values.
key_points: The topic is running an ABAP report as a different user through a background job.
The stated goal is avoiding password-based workarounds for interface or batch identity.
The post says the control is authorization object S_BTCH_NA1.
The excerpt contains no code, no field values, and no steps.
technical_details: SUBMIT <report> USER <user> VIA JOB <job> NUMBER <nr> (syntax named in title only)
Authorization object S_BTCH_NA1 (named in the post; field values not given)
30.why_it_matters: Running background work under a business user's identity is a common need. The concept is sound, but the excerpt does not show enough to use or check. Verify the authorization object and its fields in the system before relying on it.
30.developer_problem: How can a background job or interface run a report under a business user's identity without using that user's password?
30.teaching_angle: Teach the SUBMIT ... VIA JOB pattern together with the authorization model. Ask learners to check which authorization object gates the target user and what a security audit would expect. Warn against treating this as a substitute for proper technical user design.

31.summary: A short blog arguing that external systems such as Microsoft Teams or custom portals should approve SAP workflow tasks through the standard Task Processing OData service (/IWPGW/TASKPROCESSING) instead of calling the workflow API function module SAP_WAPI_DECISION_COMPLETE. The claim is that the FM approach breaks audit logs and substitution rules. The excerpt gives the claim but not the evidence, so the claim cannot be checked from the text.
key_points: The post recommends /IWPGW/TASKPROCESSING over calling SAP_WAPI_DECISION_COMPLETE directly.
It claims the FM approach breaks audit logs and substitution rules.
It does not show how those problems occur or demonstrate the OData alternative.
The excerpt contains no code, service configuration, or test results.
technical_details: SAP_WAPI_DECISION_COMPLETE (workflow API function module)
/IWPGW/TASKPROCESSING (SAP Gateway Task Processing OData service)
Workflow substitution and audit logs (named as concerns, not explained)
31.why_it_matters: Choosing the right integration path for workflow approvals matters for audit and security. The recommendation is plausible, but the post asserts its key claim without showing it. Check the behaviour on your release before adopting it.
31.developer_problem: How should an external system approve SAP workflow tasks so that audit logs and substitution rules are respected?
31.teaching_angle: Good prompt for an integration design discussion. Ask learners to compare a direct FM call with a Gateway OData call for the same approval, and to list what each path records in the workflow log. Have them test substitution behaviour in a sandbox rather than accept the claim.

32.summary: A clear, step-by-step RAP tutorial for a Task app that introduces a managed behavior definition, an action (startTask), a parameterised action (setPriority with an abstract entity), a factory action (copyTask), and a function (getDaysLeft with an abstract result). It separates changing operations (actions) from reading operations (functions) and gives a simple rule of thumb. The excerpt is cut off in the draft table, and the post has no implementation class, service definition or binding. The draft table field names also look inconsistent with the active table.
key_points: Action (startTask, completeTask, cancelTask, setPriority) changes data and is shown as a button with instance features.
Factory action copyTask creates a new instance from an existing one. It is declared with [1] and features : instance.
Function getDaysLeft only reads and returns an abstract entity result.
The behavior definition is managed, strict(2), with draft (Edit, Activate, Discard, Resume, Prepare) and an etag and lock setup.
The draft table ztask_d uses key fields mandt and taskid, but the active table uses client and task_id. A draft table normally mirrors the active table's field names, so this needs checking.
The post stops in the middle of the draft table definition, so the rest of the tutorial is missing from this excerpt.
technical_details: define table ztask (key client, key task_id sysuuid_x16); draft table ztask_d uses mandt and taskid
define root view entity ZI_Task with computed StatusText and StatusCriticality
define abstract entity ZA_TaskPriority (input) and ZA_TaskDays (result, abap.int4)
BDEF: managed implementation in class zbp_i_task unique; strict ( 2 ); with draft; lock master total etag LastChangedAt
Actions: action (features : instance) startTask result [1] $self; setPriority parameter ZA_TaskPriority
factory action (features : instance) copyTask [1]; function getDaysLeft result [1] ZA_TaskDays
Determinations: setInitialStatus on modify { create; }; validation validateTitle on save { create; update; field Title; }
Annotations: @Semantics.user.createdBy, @Semantics.systemDateTime.createdAt and localInstanceLastChangedAt
32.why_it_matters: It gives a clean mental model for choosing between action, factory action and function in RAP, which is a common interview and design question. The sample is useful for learning, but a developer copying it needs the rest of the post and must fix any draft table mismatch first.
32.developer_problem: How do I choose between RAP actions, factory actions and functions, and how do I declare each in a behavior definition?
32.teaching_angle: Strong lab material. Have learners build the Task app step by step, then implement the feature control, the determinations, and the copy logic for copyTask. Use the 'changes data vs only reads' rule as an interview question. Add a checkpoint asking learners to confirm that the draft and active table fields match.

53.summary: A blog-style technical guide to raising a custom RAP business event when a billing document is created in S/4HANA. It chains SWE2 event linkage on the billing creation event (CL_SD_BIL_BD_EVENT / VBRK), a receiver function module, a root view entity ZI_BillingDocCreated over I_BillingDocument, an abstract entity for the payload, a BDEF with an event declaration, and a behavior pool wrapper that calls RAISE ENTITY EVENT. It then describes an event binding (.evtbnd) and Enterprise Event Enablement (/IWXBE/) to publish to SAP Event Mesh or Advanced Event Mesh, with @Event.context annotations for source-side filtering. The post is truncated in the middle of the local class code, so the handler logic, the enrichment and the /IWXBE/ configuration are not shown in full.
key_points: Event trigger chain: SWE2 linkage on the billing creation event calls a receiver FM (ZSWW_WI_CREATE_VIA_EVENT_IBF), which then calls the behavior pool to raise the RAP business event.

RAP event is declared in the BDEF as 'event Created parameter ZD_BillingDocCreated' and is only raised via RAISE ENTITY EVENT inside behavior implementation code, so the post uses a public static wrapper in an ABSTRACT FINAL behavior pool class.
The abstract entity carries the payload; @Event.context with attribute and position maps selected fields (xsapbilltype, xsapsalesorg) into CloudEvents context attributes for broker-side filtering.
Verification step: use SWELS to switch on event trace, run VF01, then filter SWEL by object category CL (class), type CL_SD_BIL_BD_EVENT and event CREATED.
Publishing path: event binding artifact (.evtbnd), /IWXBE/OUTBOUND_CFG and /IWXBE/EVENT_FILTER, with target topic oneerp/Invoice/Created/v1.
technical_details: SWE2 (event type linkage), SWELS / SWEL (event trace), VF01 (billing creation)
CL_SD_BIL_BD_EVENT (class event source) and legacy BOR object VBRK
define root view entity ZI_BillingDocCreated as select from I_BillingDocument (released view), @AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED
define abstract entity ZD_BillingDocCreated with @Event.context : { attribute: 'xsapbilltype', position: 1 } and { attribute: 'xsapsalesorg', position: 2 }
BDEF: managed with unmanaged save implementation in class zbp_i_billingdoccreated unique; strict ( 2 ); lock master; authorization master ( instance ); event Created parameter ZD_BillingDocCreated;
TYPES tt_created TYPE TABLE FOR EVENT zi_billingdoccreated~created; CLASS-METHODS raise_created IMPORTING it_events TYPE tt_created
Event Binding Z_SALES_INV (.evtbnd); /IWXBE/ Enterprise Event Enablement; SAP Event Mesh / Advanced Event Mesh
Lacks release/version information (S/4HANA release, ABAP Platform version) and the full handler and error-handling code
53.why_it_matters: It shows a concrete pattern for exposing a classic billing event as a RAP business event and sending it to an event broker, which is a common clean-core need. deep_dives.title: RAP actions vs factory actions vs functions
deep_dives.explanation:
In a RAP behavior definition, an `action` changes data. A `function` only reads and returns a result, so it must not modify the instance. The tutorial declares `action (features : instance) startTask result [1] $self`, and a parameterised `action setPriority parameter ZA_TaskPriority`, where the input is an abstract entity.

A `factory action` creates a new instance from an existing one. The tutorial declares `factory action (features : instance) copyTask [1]`. Its implementation fills a create request for the new key, rather than changing the source instance. A `function getDaysLeft result [1] ZA_TaskDays` returns an abstract entity and does not change the database.

The BDEF is `managed`, `strict ( 2 )`, with `draft` and `lock master total etag LastChangedAt`. Instance feature control makes the buttons state-dependent. One caution: the draft table `ztask_d` uses `mandt` and `taskid`, while the active table uses `client` and `task_id`. A draft table normally mirrors the active table's fields, so check this before copying. The excerpt also ends mid-draft-table, so the implementation class and service binding are not shown.
key_concepts: draft table must mirror active table

deep_dives.title: Raising a RAP business event from a classic billing event
deep_dives.explanation:
The chain starts with SWE2 linkage on the billing creation event of `CL_SD_BIL_BD_EVENT`. It calls a receiver function module, which calls a public static method in the behavior pool. The method runs `RAISE ENTITY EVENT`, because RAP events can only be raised from behavior implementation code. The behavior pool is declared `ABSTRACT FINAL` and the method takes `TYPE TABLE FOR EVENT zi_billingdoccreated~created`.

The BDEF declares `event Created parameter ZD_BillingDocCreated`. The abstract entity carries the payload. `@Event.context : { attribute: 'xsapbilltype', position: 1 }` maps fields into CloudEvents context attributes, so a broker can filter without reading the payload. The root view entity selects from the released `I_BillingDocument`.

To verify, switch on the event trace in SWELS, run VF01, then check SWEL for category CL, type `CL_SD_BIL_BD_EVENT`, event CREATED. Publishing uses an `.evtbnd` event binding and `/IWXBE/` configuration (`/IWXBE/OUTBOUND_CFG`, `/IWXBE/EVENT_FILTER`). The post is truncated, so the handler logic and `/IWXBE/` setup are incomplete.

deep_dives.title: REF TO vs by-value in OO enhancement classes
deep_dives.explanation:
The question concerns `set_data` on an exit helper class, with parameters typed `vbdkr`, `nast`, `edidc`, `vbdpr_tt` and `komv_t`. The author argues that copy-on-write sharing means by-value passing costs nothing until data changes, so memory is no concern.

That is too strong. Changing to `REF TO` does not remove copying by itself, since a copy still happens when either side writes to shared data. The practical risk is semantic. The object holds a reference, so later changes by the caller become visible, and state can go stale or be shared across repeated exit calls. The exit runs several times per invoice, so this matters.

A good test: call `set_data`, modify the caller's table, and print the object's view under both signatures. Passing global data of SAP programs by reference also couples the object to the caller's data lifetime. Treat copy-on-write as an implementation detail to verify, not a language guarantee.
key_concepts: pass by value vs REF TO

post_drafts.title: RAP: action vs function vs factory action
post_drafts.text:
*RAP quick rule*

• *action* = changes data
• *function* = only reads, returns a result
• *factory action* = creates a new instance from an existing one (e.g. copyTask)

Parameters and results use abstract entities.
Instance feature control (features : instance) enables or disables the buttons.

*Check:* in a draft-enabled BDEF, the draft table fields must mirror the active table.

post_drafts.title: REF TO is not a free memory win
post_drafts.text:
*Does REF TO save memory in an OO exit class?*

Not automatically.
• A copy still happens when either side writes.
• The real risk is *aliasing*: the object sees later caller changes.
• Exits like EXIT_SAPLVEDF_002 run several times per invoice, so stale or shared state is easy to create.

Try it: call set_data, change the caller's table, then print what the object sees.

interview_questions.question: When do you use a RAP action, a factory action and a function?
interview_questions.answer: An action changes data and appears as a button, optionally with feature control per instance. A function only reads and returns a result, often an abstract entity, and must not modify the instance. A factory action creates a new instance from an existing one, as in copyTask. Parameters and results can be abstract entities. The tutorial uses `features : instance` to enable or disable the actions depending on instance state. The rule of thumb is: if it changes data, it is an action, otherwise a function.

interview_questions.question: Why does a RAP business event need a wrapper method, and how would you trigger one from a classic event?
interview_questions.answer: RAISE ENTITY EVENT can only be used inside behavior implementation code, so non-RAP code cannot raise the event directly. The pattern is a public static method in an abstract final behavior pool that takes `TYPE TABLE FOR EVENT <entity>~<event>` and raises the event. A classic event linked in SWE2 calls a receiver function module, which calls that method. The payload is an abstract entity, and @Event.context maps selected fields to CloudEvents context attributes for broker filtering. The trace can be checked in SWELS and SWEL. Publishing needs an event binding and /IWXBE/ configuration.

interview_questions.question: A teammate changes IMPORTING parameters from by-value to REF TO to save memory in an exit helper class. What do you check?
interview_questions.answer: First, whether memory is a real issue, since copy-on-write may already avoid a copy until data is changed. That is an implementation detail, not a language guarantee. With REF TO the object sees later changes made by the caller, so stale or shared state can cause bugs, especially when the exit is called several times per document. A copy still happens if either side writes to the data. Passing global data of the calling program by reference couples the object to the caller's data lifetime. I would test with a small program that changes the caller's table after set_data, and choose by design clarity unless measurements show a problem.
